Theme

Latin word

lucrum

lucrum, lucrī n.

noun, second declension

profit, gain

In this lexicon

  • profit

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Capt. 327: damnum praestet facere quam lucrum; Traupman 365: lucrum facere, make a profit

Notes

  1. 1lucrum: short u (Traupman lūcrum; Lewis & Short marks the u both long and short). De Vaan 349, s.v. lucrum: short *lu- is regular from pretonic *lh₂u-. Hor. C. 1.9.14, quem fors diērum cumque dabit, lucrō, puts lu- in a short place of the Alcaic line, where a long vowel could not stand.

Examples

  • est etiam ubi profectō damnum praestet facere quam lucrum

    there are times when it is really better to make a loss than a profitPlaut. Capt. 327

    In the entry for profit

  • namque ista subita mē jubet benignitās vigilāre, faciās nē meā culpā lucrum

    this sudden kindness tells me to stay awake, so that you don’t make a profit through my faultPhaedr. 1.23.7–8

    In the entry for profit

  • Nūllus est tam tūtus quaestus, quam quod habeās parcere.

    No profit is as safe as saving what you have.Publ. N 5
